## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Through an API

api (Amazon Bedrock) · $1.20/M blended · $0.6 in / $3 out per 1M tokens · [docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-supported.html)

<sub>[price source](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing): USD per 1M tokens, Amazon Bedrock on-demand Standard tier, Kimi K2.5 (Moonshot AI section, 'Kimi 2' table), US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio) and US West (Oregon). Priority (+75%) and Flex (-50%) tiers, cache and other regions excluded; Kimi K2.5 is not on Bedrock's model-lifecycle (legacy/EOL) page. Moonshot's own Kimi platform no longer lists kimi-k2.5. Currency: USD. Amazon Bedrock official pricing page, observed 2026-09-25. · [context source](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/blob/a668908cfe7073faa0363699486fc41a3ff52412/models/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5.toml)</sub>

### llama.cpp (recommended)

1. Install llama.cpp. Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead. [Other ways to install](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md)
   
   ```sh
   # macOS / Linux
   curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh
   # Windows
   irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

2. Run Kimi K2.5 (ud-q4_k_xl, needs ~600.5 GB, from [huggingface.co/unsloth](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF/tree/main))
   
   ```sh
   llama cli -hf unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL
   ```

3. Or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
   
   ```sh
   llama serve -hf unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL
   ```

Other versions: ud-q2_k_xl (~300.5 GB) `llama cli -hf unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL` · ud-iq1_s (~150.5 GB) `llama cli -hf unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF:UD-IQ1_S`

### LM Studio

1. Install LM Studio. Open the app once before using the lms command. [Download it (macOS / Windows / Linux)](https://lmstudio.ai/download)

2. Run Kimi K2.5 (ud-q4_k_xl, needs ~600.5 GB, from [huggingface.co/unsloth](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF/tree/main))
   
   ```sh
   lms get https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF@UD-Q4_K_XL -y
   ```

3. Then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name

Other versions: ud-q2_k_xl (~300.5 GB) `lms get https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF@UD-Q2_K_XL -y` · ud-iq1_s (~150.5 GB) `lms get https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Kimi-K2.5-GGUF@UD-IQ1_S -y` · 4bit (~657.6 GB, Mac only) `lms get https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Kimi-K2.5 -y`

### MLX (Mac)

1. Install MLX (Mac). Apple silicon Macs only, text only.
   
   ```sh
   # with uv
   uv tool install mlx-lm
   # or
   pip install mlx-lm
   ```

2. Run Kimi K2.5 (4bit, needs ~657.6 GB, Mac only, from [huggingface.co/mlx-community](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Kimi-K2.5/tree/351021afd838c866ce1a7374fce51d615773d2a8))
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.chat --model mlx-community/Kimi-K2.5
   ```

3. Or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Kimi-K2.5
   ```

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/moonshotai](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5)

[interactive version](https://whatmodel.sh/model/kimi-k2-5) · [JSON](https://whatmodel.sh/api?format=json&all=1)
